en: *Īśa-Upaniṣad* (also known as *Īśopaniṣad* or *Īśāvāsyopaniṣad*), Kāṇva recension: "By the Lord is all this covered, whatever moves in this world."
By means of that which has been renounced, you should enjoy; do not covet the wealth of anyone whatsoever.
"Performing actions here in this world, one should desire to live for a hundred years;
thus it is with you, and not otherwise than this—action does not cling to a person. (Īśa Upaniṣad 2)
"Sunless indeed are those worlds, enveloped in blind darkness;
to them go after death those people who are slayers of the Self. (Īśa Upaniṣad 3)
One thing moves not, yet it is swifter than the mind; the gods could not overtake it as it sped on before them.
It stands still, yet it outstrips others who run; in it Mātariśvan places the waters.
It moves, and it moves not; it is far, and it is near;
it is within all this, and it is outside of all this.
But he who perceives all beings in the Self alone,
and the Self in all beings, does not feel aversion because of that.
When for the one who perceives all beings have become the Self alone,
what delusion and what sorrow can there be for him who beholds this oneness?
He has pervaded all—pure, bodiless, woundless, without sinews, clean, unpierced by evil;
the seer, the wise, the encompassing, the self-existent, who from the beginning of eternal years has established the objects of reality according to their true nature.
Into blind darkness enter those who worship ignorance;
into even greater darkness, as it were, than that, enter those who delight in knowledge alone.
"Other indeed they call that which is attained through knowledge, and other that which is attained through ignorance"—thus have we heard from the wise who explained this to us. (IsUp 10)
He who knows both knowledge and ignorance together—
having crossed over death by means of ignorance, he enjoys immortality through knowledge.
Into blind darkness enter those who worship the Unmanifest;
into even greater darkness, as it were, than that, enter those who delight in the Manifest.
"They say that [the world] is one thing through manifestation, and they say it is another through non-manifestation;
thus have we heard from the wise who explained this to us. (IsUp 13)
He who knows both origin and destruction together—having crossed over death by means of destruction, he attains immortality through origin. (IsU 14)
The face of truth is covered by a golden vessel;
O Pūṣan, uncover it for me, so that I, whose nature is truth, may see. (IsUp 15)
O Pūṣan, sole seer, Yama, Sūrya, son of Prajāpati! Spread out your rays and gather together your splendor.
That form of yours which is most beautiful—that I behold. That person who is yonder, that am I. (IsU 16)
The wind has departed as the immortal breath; this body ends in ashes.
Om! O Kratu, remember; remember what was done. O Kratu, remember; remember what was done. (IsU 17)
O Agni, lead us by a good path to prosperity, O God who knowest all ways;
remove from us the sin that leads astray, and we shall offer unto thee the most abundant word of homage. (IsUp 18)
